sentences.text: Garamaudo bauciensis is estimated to have been about 2.5 m long.
Its limbs and pelvic girdle were more primitive and lacked the paddle-like flippers seen in later mosasaurids.
The generic name Garamaudo derives from a Provençal phrase meaning “beware the cursed one”.
The specific epithet bauciensis honors the type locality Bouc-Bel-Air.
Fossils of Garamaudo were recovered from the Aix-en-Provence Basin at the Bouc-Bel-Air – Sousquières locality in southeastern France.
The most complete specimen, designated the holotype, comprises roughly 20 skeletal elements and was collected in 1997.
The species was formally described in 2026 in Peer Community Journal by Nathalie Bardet and colleagues.
Osteosclerosis—bone thickening—present in the fossils suggests Garamaudo could dive to shallow depths.
Its hunting strategy is inferred to have relied on ambush rather than rapid acceleration.
Garamaudo bauciensis is the sole species assigned to the genus Garamaudo.
Phylogenetic analysis places it in an unresolved clade within the subfamily Tethysaurinae, alongside Pannoniasaurus, Tethysaurus and an unnamed taxon.
Garamaudo lived during the Late Cretaceous Santonian age in freshwater deposits of France.
